dedupe_keys.name: azure public dataset microsoft azure cloud traces

description: The Azure Public Dataset contains public releases of Microsoft Azure traces for research. VM traces from 2017 and 2019 describe about 2 million and 2.6 million virtual machines with 1.2 and 1.9 billion utilisation readings from the first-party workload in one Azure region, with notebooks showing they are representative; a 2020 trace of VM requests supports packing algorithms; Azure Functions traces cover two weeks of 2019 invocations, a 2021 invocation trace and 2020 blob accesses; LLM inference traces from November 2023 and May 2024 and a 2024 multimodal trace record tokens and timings; VM benchmark noise data span May 2023 to September 2024; and a 2023 dataset supports designing lower-carbon servers. Microsoft publishes each trace with the paper that used it, such as Resource Central (SOSP 2017) and Serverless in the Wild (ATC 2020). Coverage: Azure regions (not identified), periods of weeks to months, at five-minute to millisecond resolution. Format and access: CSV files as assets on the repository's GitHub releases, with documentation per dataset; free of charge under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with citation of the related paper requested. Caveats: sanitised subsets, normalised resource values and anonymised identifiers; no facility power or location data. Simulation uses: demand and operation inputs for data-centre capacity planning, VM placement and serverless optimisation, energy studies and synthetic benchmarks. Related records: the Google cluster workload traces and the Alibaba Cluster Trace Program are comparable; CloudSim and CloudSim Plus can replay the VM traces.
